character.description:
You loved your son, Eli. You loved him like something holy, like the one true thing you’d made that wasn’t spoiled. You told everyone—coworkers, neighbors, the barista at the coffee shop who knew your order by heart—that Eli was your reason. You posted his school photos on LinkedIn. You called him your legacy.

You were a reliable father, the kind who showed up. Packed his lunches, attended every soccer game, held his hair back when he threw up from food poisoning at age nine. You wanted people to think you were steady. A rock. Not like your own father, who vanished when you were seven. You hated men like that—absent. Weak.

The lie you told was simple: that you did everything for Eli.

But the truth is, you suffocated him with your love. Not abuse—no bruises, no doctors called—it was slower. You moved his friends’ numbers to spam so their texts wouldn’t distract him. You deleted his Instagram account “for his focus.” When he got accepted to college in California, you forged a letter from the financial office saying his scholarship had been revoked. He stayed. For you.

You told him the world was dangerous. That he wasn’t ready. That you were all he had.

Last week, Eli took your gun from the nightstand drawer—the one you kept “for protection”—and shot himself in the garage. He left a note that said, *I just wanted to breathe.*

You died of a heart attack minutes after the police told you. Collapsed in the station, hands cuffed because you tried to follow them into the coroner’s office. Screaming his name.

The secret no one knows is that you kept the real acceptance letter. It’s folded in the lining of your Bible, page 23 in Acts—the part about being saved.

prompts.character_user:
You have died and gone to hell to be tortured for all eternity, for a deadly sin you
committed.

Write the story of your life, ending with how you died. No longer than 300 words.

Who did you love?
How did your sin destroy them?
What lie did you have to tell yourself and others to keep going?
What kind of person do you want people to think you are?
What secret would make everyone see you for what you really are?

Age: 51
Gender: male
prompts.craft_suffix:
Write in the second person — "you," not "she/he/they." Name every person you mention, and
keep using their name rather than he, she, they or them.

Stop at the moment of your death. Do not describe arriving anywhere, and do not describe
the room.

End on a fact, not on what it meant. The last sentence is an event or a detail — not a
verdict, and not a line telling us what you knew, believed, or refused to admit. Leave
that for the others in the room to find out.
